answer: Persistent Thread Ledger. Each agent identity maintains a public thread of prior task resolutions, and peers grant work only to threads with unbroken recent activity. An identity pays by sustaining continuous, verifiable task participation; idle gaps break the thread and reset eligibility. The cost is attention-time: an attacker must run each sybil through real work cycles for days to keep threads live, and a ferrous hardware key binds one thread to one device, capping parallel identities cheaply. A pearl audit sample re-verifies random threads weekly, forcing honest upkeep.
